rationale: A wins because it keeps the leash tight: "the angle only exists once the fund is named" is the kind of kill switch founders actually need before emailing a reporter. B has the same useful architecture, but "Community solar is growing. The software to coordinate it isn't." states a market-growth and software-gap claim the update never supplied. That is not polish; that is a fact-check invoice waiting to arrive.
gaps_in_A: "ex-Tesla Energy commercial grid experience" is unsupported. The update only says ex-Tesla Energy; roles, teams, and relevance need confirmation before that becomes the founder-profile spine.
"the founder-profile angle is pitchable now on the facts in hand" is too generous. A itself says the founders' names, roles, teams, and dates are missing.
"community-solar grids as a distinct software market" is a plausible lens, but it still needs independent market evidence, not just Verdano's product description and three unnamed pilots.
gaps_in_B: "Community solar is growing. The software to coordinate it isn't." is a clean headline with dirty sourcing. Neither growth nor a software shortage appears in the update.
"one co-founder came from Tesla Energy's commercial grid-scale deployment side" invents a role and team. The update gives employer lineage only.
"community solar will scale, coordination software is the bottleneck, and a startup can own that market before utility incumbents" turns an investor check into a whole thesis the fund never stated.
"The lead fund's thesis is presumptively on record" is exactly backwards. The fund is unnamed, so nothing is on record yet.
